subject.title: feat: let plugins control inbound debounce policy

question: Should OpenClaw expose a generic public `inbound_debounce` plugin hook now, or solve the demonstrated need with a bounded WhatsApp-owned per-conversation policy?
rationale: Both this PR and the open alternative address the same debounce need with incompatible long-term contracts. Choosing either determines plugin SDK compatibility commitments, channel ownership, and the operator-facing configuration model.

options.title: Adopt the bounded WhatsApp surface
options.body: Sponsor the owner-scoped WhatsApp per-conversation policy and keep generic SDK debounce control out of the public contract until more channels require it.

options.title: Sponsor the generic plugin hook
options.body: Approve this SDK contract explicitly, document its cross-channel ownership expectations, and require real WhatsApp proof before merge.

options.title: Defer both contract proposals
options.body: Close or pause both implementations until maintainers have a broader multi-channel debounce design and ownership decision.

recommendation.title: Adopt the bounded WhatsApp surface
recommendation.body: Sponsor the owner-scoped WhatsApp per-conversation policy and keep generic SDK debounce control out of the public contract until more channels require it.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only repository member in the supplied discussion who acknowledged responsibility for reviewing this contract choice.
